preconditions.description: The number of computers n is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.
The number of existing cables m is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each existing cable connects two valid computer indices between 1 and n.
The input contains exactly m cable definitions.

postconditions.description: The total number of cables in the output is at least the number of original cables.
The number of printed cable lines matches the declared total p.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in output_cables)
postconditions.description: Every output cable connects two valid computer indices.
The set of output cables, when direction is ignored, contains all original cables (accounting for multiplicity).

postconditions.expression: all(sum(1 for u, v in output_cables if u == node) % 2 == 0 and sum(1 for u, v in output_cables if v == node) % 2 == 0 for node in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: For every computer, the number of outgoing cables is even and the number of incoming cables is even, allowing perfect pairing of same-direction cables.
The total number of cables p is the minimum possible value satisfying the even-degree constraints for all nodes.
